verdict: NOT READY TO BUILD (check-nose, A15, read-only, 6.4 min: start 1792324999, end 1792325380). The anatomy is sound and the sourcing is mostly honest. The dish is replaced by a bent passage, and the ala, alar fold, groove and philtrum are all cited. No OPEN Phase 1 number is used as a reference: the L whole-rim proof margin appears only as the planted dish depth 2.31 mm, and the eye OPEN items are unused. C6b, C13 and C14 are ear and whisker criteria and do not apply to the nose; the fur-parting handoff along the philtrum is recorded. Units and frame are consistent: scale 1.80 m / 5184 px = 0.347 mm/px, look-down asin(0.236) = 13.7 deg, and the R/L sign convention holds. I checked the vestibule clearances on a small Tripo crop of 6k vertices: the wall is at least 1.9 mm from the outer skin, and the only nearer surface is the dish, which Step 0 removes. However, 4 of the 11 probes fail or pass on the wrong build when tested against the spec's own numbers, and the crease conflicts with approved C3b. Under A10 the probes are not yet valid. Scratch scripts (analytic ray model, crop clearance) are in %TEMP%\p2prep_check-nose\ (ray.py, clr.py, clr2.py); no project files were written.
blocking: vestibule_depth_ray cannot pass on the spec's own lumen. It requires every ray in a 10 deg cone about T0 to travel at least 5.0 mm. An analytic model of the spec's centreline (34.8 deg / 33.5 deg bend at P1) and its stations (a 1.6/1.2/1.0, b 1.3/0.8/0.7) gives free lengths of 3.0-4.7 mm (R) and 2.98-4.84 mm (L); the axis ray itself gets only 3.62 mm. Adding the 0.7 mm alar-fold ridge lowers that to 1.6-4.9 mm, with 0 of 50 rays reaching 5 mm. The bend that vestibule_hidden_end requires is what makes this test impossible. Fix: measure the air path along the centreline (at least 8 mm) plus an axis ray of at least 3.0 mm, which is still more than the 2.31 mm dish.

leather_outline fails on its own build target. The probe asks for a projected bbox of 45 x 29 px +-2 px. The spec's own registration projects the Phase 1 leather['0'] outline, which the build must match within 0.5 mm, to 47.6 x 31.9 px: 2.6 and 2.9 px out. A correct build therefore fails.

The philtrum probe contradicts the recipe. Step 5 sweeps the groove through leather_tip (-0.94, -69.72, -16.3), which is nose.json's lowest outline point and lies off the midline (x -0.31..-0.76 at z -15.5..-15.8). The probe requires the section minimum within |x + 0.2| <= 0.4 mm. At z -16.3 the groove sits at |x + 0.2| = 0.74, so a correct build fails. Fix: use a midline waypoint (x -0.2) at the tip height instead of the outline extreme.

The ala_outer probe cannot catch its planted 'no ala' failure. The pass window is a crown 0.4-0.9 mm proud of the alar-groove floor, but the groove alone is cut 0.3-0.5 mm deep. With no ala at all, crown-over-floor equals the groove depth, which falls in the window whenever the depth is 0.4-0.5 mm. The second check, the photo-render crescent area (+-35 pct), depends on lighting that the spec itself says 'cannot be separated from geometry'. Fix: measure crown height against the Step-0 patched surface, not the groove floor.

The leather/bridge crease valley conflicts with approved C3b. The spec adds a 0.2-0.4 mm valley 0.3-1.2 mm outside the outline, on haired skin where d > 0, and its crease probe requires 'one valley >= 0.15 mm deep'. C3b forbids exactly this ('no rings or creases where coat regions meet'), and it is C3b's planted failure. The valley's only source is ESTIMATE, and the spec's own photo note says 'no separate crease line visible'. Remove the valley and keep the coat-inset step, or get the person's ruling.
should: C3 conflict: furless leather must sit ON the envelope within +-0.5 mm, but Step 0 (dish patch, up to 2.15/2.31 mm off Tripo) and Step 1 (ala crown) move it on purpose. Declare a C3 exclusion mask (each rim dilated 1 mm, plus the ala ellipsoids), or C3's 'bump/hole' check fails the correct nose. Likewise give C3b's groove-band relief check an exclusion for the philtrum (0.45-0.8 mm deep under fur, which is anatomy, not fur relief).

The e2 rule is wrong for R. The text says e2 = n_out x e1, which for R gives (0.068, 0.42, -0.905), pointing ventral. The listed R value (-0.07, -0.42, 0.9) is n_in x e1; L does match n_out x e1. This is mirror handedness: state the rule per side. A builder who recomputes from the text puts the R slit offset and the ala on the wrong side.

The Step-0 patch straddles the furless/haired step. The R and L rims come within 0.08 and 0.11 mm of the leather outline, and 97/106 R and 84/92 L rim points lie within 3 mm of it. So the 1 mm dilation and the rim+1..rim+3 thin-plate fitting ring sample haired skin that is inset about 1.2 mm. Restrict the fitting samples to the d = 0 leather, or patch the envelope before the inset.

nostril_opening sections the surface with a PLANE 0.3 mm inside the rim plane. The rim is exactly planar (residual 0.00), but the slit is only extruded to 0.5 mm below a convex patched surface. Wherever the patch bulges more than 0.2 mm above the rim plane, the section misses the slit and sees only the vestibule ellipse: e1 ratio about 3.2/9.0 = 0.36 against the required 0.65-0.80. Section an offset surface 0.3 mm under the built skin instead. (PLAUSIBLE; the bulge is unbuilt, but the leather curvature makes 0.3-1 mm likely.)

The slit tail is a 0.5 mm-deep blind notch, a dish in miniature. From H to open_end is 4.41 mm (R) and 3.40 mm (L), while the lumen's semi-axis a is only 1.6 / 1.4 mm. That leaves about 2.8 mm (R) and 2.0 mm (L) of open slit with no passage behind it. No probe checks that the open part leads into the lumen; the ray probe only fires from H. Widen the lumen along e1 for s < 1.5, or probe it.

Photo-probe tolerances are tighter than the registration. The philtrum end allows 1.5 px and the groove and nostril paths 2 px, but the spec rates its own translation-only registration at about 1 mm (about 3 px), and the leather bbox misfit is 2.6-2.9 px. Widen the tolerances to at least 3 px, or fix the camera-to-head transform first (the spec's own OPEN item).

Values with no source or confidence: the vestibule clearances (septum 2.0, outer skin 1.5, mouth 3.0 mm), the slit taper (0.3 mm half-width at 70 pct of rim length) and head_lip_round 0.3 mm. Flag each as ESTIMATE with a confidence (G2).

The L outer extent rests on weak photo support. The photo shows a dark core of only 2.8 x 2.1 mm plus a faint tail at lum 130-180, against a projected rim of 5.22 x 4.61 mm. Rate the L comma extent low, not medium, and note that REVIEW_nose B1 found opening size and asymmetry setting-dependent in v1 (cav 0.3: R 9.19 vs L 8.92 mm long).
The grid memory claim is wrong at the fine end. 0.08 mm over x[-14,14] y[-76,-50] z[-26,0] is 350 x 325 x 325 = 37 M voxels, about 148 MB float32. Only 0.10 mm (76 MB) meets the stated <= 80 MB.

The ala_outer render probe does not say which lights or render settings to use, so it is not reproducible. The dish_removed probe runs on the Step-0 intermediate surface, while _note says probes run on the built surface. State which surface each probe reads.

The Y junction is lifted onto a straight chord to Tripo's mouth midline, and that mouth is the V-groove artefact (REVIEW_mouth). The point is snapped to the surface later in Step 5, but its y (tol 0.8) inherits the chord. Keep it OPEN until the mouth spec agrees (the spec already lists this).
